notes: No amp+cab block — running into tube amp. Confirmed rig: Ed O'Brien used a 1964 Gibson ES-335, Voodoo Lab Sparkle Drive, Boss DD5 delay, and Akai Headrush E2 looper through a Mesa Boogie Trem-O-Verb and Vox AC30. Thom Yorke used a 1964 Gibson SG. Jonny played totally clean with just a Gretsch Tennessee Rose, Akai Headrush E1 looper, and small vintage Orpheum amplifier. Two delays approximate the dual-delay/looper setup — Delay 1 is the primary dotted eighth (exact match at 87 BPM), Delay 2 is a secondary dotted sixteenth creating rhythmic interlocking shimmer. Teemah! approximates Sparkle Drive — BYPASSED in S1, ACTIVE in S2 as song intensifies.
note_on_block_limit: Seven blocks — at the eight-block limit. Two Simple Delay blocks used for the dual-delay texture. If Helix LT does not allow two instances of the same delay model, substitute the secondary Simple Delay with an Adriatic Delay or Cosmos Echo.

noise_gate.notes: Very open gate — delicate arpeggio tone. Natural decay essential.

overdrive.notes: Approximates Voodoo Lab Sparkle Drive. BYPASSED in Snapshot 1 (clean arpeggios). ACTIVE in Snapshot 2 as song intensifies around the 2:30 mark — very low gain, just warmth and slight compression. NOTE: Bass Cut and Treble Cut are CUT controls — higher values remove more frequency.

modulation.notes: Very subtle chorus adds slight width and shimmer — the three-dimensional bloom of the arpeggio tone. Speed very slow, Depth low — should feel like natural animation not obvious chorus. ACTIVE in both snapshots, slightly more prominent in Snapshot 2.

eq.notes: Gentle EQ shaping. Slight mid boost adds body and presence to arpeggiated notes so they cut through the dual-delay wash. Snapshot 2 slightly warms high mid to compensate for Teemah! coloring.

delay_primary.notes: PRIMARY DELAY — approximates Boss DD5 set to dotted eighth. Tempo-synced to 87 BPM. Dotted eighth = 517ms — exact match (0.2ms off). This is the defining effect of the song — Mix at 45-50% makes delay structural, not supportive. High Mix is intentional. Feedback increases in S2 as song densifies.

delay_secondary.notes: SECONDARY DELAY — approximates Akai Headrush E2 looper used for additional texture. Tempo-synced to 87 BPM. Dotted sixteenth = 259ms (original target 276ms, 17ms off — synced value preferred). The two delays (517ms d1/8 + 259ms d1/16) create rhythmically interlocking repeat pattern filling gaps between primary repeats — this is the shimmer making the song sound like multiple guitars.

reverb.notes: Long, lush reverb — this song lives in space. Snapshot 1 more reverberant and atmospheric. Snapshot 2 pulls slightly tighter as song intensifies to prevent dual-delay texture from becoming too washy.

1_verse.description: Clean shimmering arpeggio tone. Teemah! bypassed. Two interlocking delays at 45% and 22% mix create illusion of multiple guitar parts. Long reverb at 38% mix.

2_intense.description: Late-song intense version (approx 2:30 mark). Teemah! active for warmth on longer sustained notes. Primary delay opens to 50% mix. Reverb tightens slightly to maintain definition.

playing_notes.pickup_notes: Neck pickup throughout — warm and glassy
playing_notes.technique: Pick very lightly near soundhole. Allow notes to ring into each other rather than keeping them cleanly separated. Two delays together mean TIMING IS EVERYTHING — practice the arpeggio pattern at 87 BPM before engaging delays.
playing_notes.snapshot_cues: Snapshot 1 for main arpeggiated sections. Switch to Snapshot 2 around the 2:30 mark when arrangement thickens and O'Brien moves to longer sustained notes.
playing_notes.timing_critical: Primary delay at 45-50% Mix means any rhythmic inconsistency in picking is audible in repeats and compounds through the secondary delay. Metronomic precision is required.
